hoeschec wrote: A good question to start asking myself when looking for a good LS kink:

Where is the bait for the herd?

Fishermen use bait to attract fish to their pole.....it is the same for IT's. IT's need to entice traders to get on the wrong side of the trade.

The best LS is probably located somewhere below the bait level on a bullish setup and just above the bait level on a bearish setup.

Brilliant analogy. My favourite is a invisible kink which is still deep enough to trick the retailers. Like a kink that relates to a monthly area that can only be seen on 1m chart. Love those ones. especially with a highly visible cap at the FTB. Brilliant bait

Once again, thank you for taking the time to read through my journal and help out! I am glad to see there are traders who are understanding this!

Now for a bit of personal venting....

I think I am going through a low point in my journey lately. I spent an unbelievable amount of time studying since September 2016 (in some bases 12+ hours a day). My journal only reflects a small amount of the work I'm actually completing. I made some giant leaps forward in my understanding of the market, and focused on Salivan and Omid's philosophy and application of RTM principles. But Unfortunately, Salivan and Omid aren't posting on RTM anymore (or maybe they are on a break).

Then there was the Academy Lite course (which I wasn't able to attend) and there seems to be a whole new set of information and names/abbreviations etc... and it seems like I am starting back on at square one again. The concepts of a FL not being a FL until its target has been met was never discussed here until recently. Kinks were never discussed until recently. QM's were always a part of the RTM way of reading price, but now it seems that it's all we talk about. It wasn't that way before (at least it didn't seem that way before). I feel like I am the only one who is feeling frustrated with this and I am Mr. Rookie again!

Maybe there is a correlation between the old concepts and some of the newer concepts IF has been introducing lately. Maybe I just have not been able to put the pieces together.

I want to make it absolutely clear that I LOVE the hard work. I look forward to it every day. I just want to see continual improvement..and lately I have plateaued....or even taken a few steps back.

I am ashamed of my reliance on Salivan and Omid - good traders should never put their success/failure on other traders! I am responsible for my own journey and my own highs and lows. This has been a tough (but necessary) lesson for me to learn.

This constant confusion makes me feel like I'm chasing my tail. Lots of effort but no progress. The days turn in to weeks, the weeks turn in to months, and the months turn in to years. Still sitting here, and still confused, always hoping the next study session will reveal something new which will put me on the path to profitability.

So from what I am reading, it seems the best LS is one that breaks an important FL.

Here is an example on GBP-USD:

I found a good FL...there was a break of this FL and I marked that as a LS. Price breaks the LS to the upside, and RT back. The main bounce occurs at a kink...but not at the LS kink..it seems to bounce at the high that forms just prior to the LS. That high didn't engulf anything important, so why did price bonce so strongly from its kink?
It was an ignored LS that formed a kink. On return, you got the bounce because orders were left behind.

Hoeschec, Look to the left of my bottom green line. See how it ENG the FL limit to the left of it? Therefore, once that was ENG, we formed an UFL. My 2 green line is an UFL. The top green line is my LS of the H&S pattern. Remember in video 2, once we get an ENG of FL, we need to mark the bottom and top of the FL and look for PA there This was a beautiful setup because the upper green line happened to be a LS of the new H&S pattern and when price came to that LS level, it should have bounce down. But instead, it broke to the upside. The kink was created after it broke up. So now it becomes like a flip zone. There we now have orders there waiting for the long trade up and that is exactly what we got.

I want to revisit this post from Gslao:

The first engulf:

The low of the engulf and the extent of the RT creates the Upper Flag Limit (UFL).

The Upper flag limit line was broken twice...the first time it was broken (labeled as the Head in Gslao's drawing) there was no trade on its RT to the LS kink (see blue circle in chart below). How did you know not to trade the RT to the kink after the first break of the LS? Do we always wait for a 'head' to form on the first break of a LS?

The second time price breaks the LS and the head of the H&S pattern. When price RT to the kink the trade is taken: See the orange circle:

So, it seems to me the following steps must be taken in order:

(for a bullish kink bounce)

1. Find a strong opposing FL that is broken. Mark low and high of the break. The high of the break is the UFL.

2. This UFL is the LS

3. Wait for this UFL (LS) to be broken to the upside. This break forms the head (RS)

4. Wait for price to RT to the LS line after breaking and forming the Head/RS.

5. We would expect a reaction at the LS (to fulfill the H&S pattern). Wait for this H&S to be ignored

6. Ignoring of the HS pattern creates a new high...this time breaking above the original LS and the Head/RS

7. Draw the Kink for the LS and prepare for price to return to this kink

8. We expect residual order flow to exist in this kink after price ignores the HS pattern, and we buy when price returns to this kink

I am going to show this in a drawing step by step in the next post.

Hopefully I am understanding the order of events...Feel free to tell me if I am wrong...thanks for everyone's help

Step by step drawing - bullish kink setup:

Step 1: Price engulfs an opposing FL

Step 2: Mark the low of the engulf and the furthest extent of the RT before a new low is made. This is the Upper FL:

Step 3:: Wait for a new high to form above the UFL/LS. This is the 'head' of our HS Pattern and it is also the RS level that will act as bait for retailers trying to buy the bullish swap level.

Step 4: Price approaches the LS of the H&S but does not react... it ignores this level.

Step 5: Price makes a new high after ignoring the H&S Pattern. This is when we really want to start preparing for an entry. Watch price as it returns to the LS below...

Step 6: Look at the LS and the IHSP (Ignored H&S pattern). Go to LTF and draw the most accurate kink possible. Use tick chart data if needed. Look for last place where price crossed this important line. Draw the kink/FTR and look to make sure it has fresh order flow (make sure orders haven't been consumed already).

Step 7: Look for PA as price approaches the kink. Ideally there will be some kind of compression or Diamond setup on LTF to indicate IT's are preparing to buy. We buy when price RT to the kink.

Some of these kinks have HUGE bounces...massive R:R.

If we can learn to consistently choose the best kinks we will make some amazing trades. The hard part is finding the best LS to draw that kink from....

NZD-USD Simulation Trade:

This might be one of the best simulation trades I've done in a long time.

Every time I get frustrated I comes across one of these beauties and I start feeling motivated again. Can you imagine being skilled enough to trade one or two of these setups each week? Jeez...

This chart pretty much says it all.... hard part is doing this live.

I think the key to this trade being successful is having a met target below, when price is coming from an unmet target for buyers (target is ORFL - Down and that is the green rectangle).

By far the most challenging part of trading: knowing where the relevant targets are located.

* You will not buy if price is coming from a reached target for buyers

* You will not sell if price is coming from a reached target for sellers

* You buy if price is coming from an unreached target for buyers

* You sell if price is coming from an unreached target for sellers

Logically this makes total sense.

The hard part is drawing the relevant targets correctly...

Also, knowing if the target has been met. For example: if targets are FL they have an MPL. Is a target met if price reaches the FL but has not consumed the extreme set of orders in its MPL

Just some thoughts I want to write down for future reference:

IQM or IHS (Ignored Head and Shoulders) are great places to look for a trade when price returns to the LS kink.

Major questions to ask when determining whether or not to trade the bounce:

(not sure this is accurate, but I want to write it down anyway)

Assuming bullish trade:

1. Is the LS formed after engulfing an opposing FL

2. Look at the engulf that preceded the LS. That engulf (like every engulf) has a target. Was that target met? If we are looking for a long trade, we want any downside engulf to already hit its target (that way we feel confident price has no reason to drop below our proposed entry)

3. Look at the RS Level (HH or LL of the IQM). Is there an engulf to the upside that still needs to reach an upside target? If so, price is coming from an unmet target for buyers. this is good news if we are looking to take a long trade at a kink.

This IQM didn't work very well. The LS is shown, and we don't get a nice bounce at the kink. It looks like price was coming from a met target for buyers which explains why price broke the kink. Don't take longs when price is coming from a met target for longs.
